response.title: Can I connect a newer expansion battery to an older power station of the same brand, or do they have to match?
response.answer:
Yes, you can sometimes connect a newer expansion battery to an older power station from the same brand, but compatibility depends on the exact models.

They don't necessarily have to be from the same generation. However, being the same brand does not guarantee compatibility.

Manufacturers such as EcoFlow, BLUETTI, Anker, and Jackery use different battery communication protocols, voltages, and connectors across product generations.

What determines compatibility?

Factor

	

Why it matters




Battery voltage

	

Must be supported by the power station




Communication protocol

	

The power station must recognize and manage the battery




Connector and cable

	

Must be electrically compatible, not just physically fit




Firmware

	

Some combinations require firmware updates




Manufacturer support

	

Determines whether the combination is officially supported

Even if two batteries have the same connector, they may not work together. Using an unsupported combination could damage equipment or create a safety hazard.

Examples

BLUETTI: Its newer B500K expansion battery supports several older power stations, including the AC300 and AC200MAX, with the appropriate connection setup. 
5,120Wh - BLUETTI US

EcoFlow: Some expansion batteries work across different models, but others are model-specific. EcoFlow publishes a compatibility guide.
